title: Materials research with a general-purpose agent
authors: Paulo R. Pires, Théo Cavignac, Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Hai-Chen Wang, Silvana Botti, Miguel A. L. Marques
abstract: Over the last decade we have built Alexandria, an open database of about 15 million density-functional calculations of crystals. It includes PBE, PBEsol, SCAN and TB-mBJ results, structures relaxed at pressures up to 150 GPa, dielectric tensors and about 145,000 electron-phonon calculations, together with more than 400 million structures relaxed with machine-learned potentials. On these data we trained a generative model for crystal structures, a universal interatomic potential and graph neural networks for more than ten properties, from band gaps to superconducting critical temperatures. From the convex hull we computed a reaction graph of the 17.4 billion reactions between its 193,416 stable compounds. Here we give all of this to a general-purpose language-model agent. Working unattended, the agent screens the database for a solar absorber, drops a candidate whose synthesis releases too little energy, and writes a synthesis plan with precursors, crucible and atmosphere. Asked about the well-studied Ba-Zr-S system, it finds an unreported sulfide and designs the experiment that would confirm or rule it out. Asked for an air-stable alternative, it designs one and tests it against new structures from the generative model. With web search alone, the same agent proposes what the literature already discusses. Put together, the data, the models and the reaction graph let a general agent do what none of them does alone: go from a question in plain words to an experiment that a laboratory can run and test.

infographic.key_insight: A general-purpose language-model agent links materials data, predictive models and reaction networks to turn plain-language research questions into testable synthesis plans.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Integrated screening and synthesis planning could help engineers identify functional materials while considering reaction energetics and practical laboratory conditions.
method: Connect the agent to Alexandria’s crystal calculations and trained materials models.
Use a reaction graph to assess candidate stability and synthesis energetics.
Generate synthesis plans and challenge proposed materials with newly generated structures.
infographic.evidence_signal: Using about 15 million density-functional calculations and a 17.4-billion-reaction graph, the agent produced unattended case studies covering solar absorbers, an unreported Ba–Zr–S sulfide and an air-stable alternative; web search alone returned literature-discussed proposals.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports computational proposals and experimental plans, not laboratory validation of the predicted materials or synthesis routes.
infographic.paper_title: Materials research with a general-purpose agent

title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
authors: Abhijit Biswas, Eugenio Garcia-Granados, Saman Zare, Mozhdeh Mirakhory, JungHun Park, Shuvodeep De
abstract: Ceramic materials that maintain structural integrity and resist thermal-shock under extreme conditions are critical for many applications. Here we show that spark plasma sintered composites containing equal weight fractions of hexagonal silicon carbide (6H-SiC) and boron nitride (h-BN) exhibit exceptional stability under extreme high-temperature oxidizing conditions and unusually stable temperature-independent thermal conductivity across a broad temperature range. Under high-velocity oxygen-fuel torch exposure in air, it withstands prolonged heating and thermal-cycling at surface temperatures reaching >1500 °C, whereas pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractures or erodes. Microstructural evaluation shows the formation of a multi-phase surface silica layer that further protects the material from oxidation. Finite-element analysis heat-flux map shows that intrinsic porosity mitigates thermal stress, while ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations reveal thermally driven interfacial reconstruction and the formation of a Si-N/C-B-rich bonding network, enhancing the interfacial cohesion at elevated temperatures. This lightweight, easily machinable ceramic composite will be a promising structural material in extreme environment applications.

infographic.key_insight: A spark-plasma-sintered composite with equal weight fractions of 6H-SiC and h-BN withstands extreme oxidizing heat while maintaining unusually temperature-independent thermal conductivity.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This lightweight, machinable ceramic is a promising candidate for structural components exposed to severe heat and thermal cycling.
method: Spark plasma sintering of equal-weight 6H-SiC/h-BN mixtures.
High-velocity oxygen-fuel torch testing and microstructural evaluation.
Finite-element heat-flux analysis and ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations.
infographic.evidence_signal: The composite survived prolonged heating and thermal cycling at surface temperatures above 1500 °C, while pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractured or eroded.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not quantify exposure duration, cycle count, or retained mechanical strength, limiting assessment of service lifetime.
infographic.paper_title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability

title: Brute-force molecular dynamics simulation of aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$
authors: Elisa Petroni, Dario Baratella, Omar Abou El Kheir, Andrea Redaelli, Marco Bernasconi
abstract: Chalcogenide alloys such as the prototypical Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ compound are used in phase change electronic memories due to their ability to undergo a fast and reversible transition between the amorphous and crystalline phases upon heating. The amorphous phase is subject to aging that leads to an increase in the electrical resistance, which is detrimental to the operation of the devices. Using a machine learning interatomic potential, we have investigated the structural relaxations responsible for aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ in molecular dynamics simulations at temperatures slightly below the glass transition. The aging simulation, lasting about 100 ns, follows an equilibration of 24 ns at 400 K. During aging we observed an enhancement of the Peierls distortion in axial bonds which is a typical feature of these alloys that we relate to the widening of the electronic band gap computed within Density Functional Theory in smaller aged amorphous models. We also observed a marked reduction of the atomic mobility with an increase of the bond lifetimes during aging. However, we do not see a reduction in homopolar bonds, which are expected to be absent in the ideal aged glass and which should be removed on a much longer time scale.

infographic.key_insight: Machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics links aging in amorphous Ge₂Sb₂Te₅ to stronger axial-bond Peierls distortion, a wider electronic band gap, and reduced atomic mobility.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Understanding these structural changes could help address aging-related resistance drift in phase-change memory devices.
method: Use a machine-learning interatomic potential for molecular dynamics.
Simulate about 100 ns of aging after 24 ns of equilibration at 400 K.
Compute electronic band gaps with density functional theory in smaller aged amorphous models.
infographic.evidence_signal: The simulations show enhanced Peierls distortion and longer bond lifetimes during aging, while density functional theory calculations indicate band-gap widening.
infographic.watch_item: Homopolar bonds did not decrease within the simulated window; their removal may require much longer timescales.
infographic.paper_title: Brute-force molecular dynamics simulation of aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$

title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
authors: Jiang Yuhan, Matthew Otten
abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

infographic.key_insight: QMage proposes a coherent quantum search for crystal configurations whose first-principles properties meet specified targets within a chosen tolerance.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could support targeted materials discovery where classical property calculations or data-driven extrapolation are unreliable.
method: Search over atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions.
Block-encode each configuration’s Hamiltonian, isolate a target eigenstate, and evaluate properties coherently.
Amplify configurations meeting property targets with fixed-point search, then measure candidates.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports logical-qubit and Toffoli-depth estimates spanning a classically routine benchmark and harder targets, rather than demonstrated materials discovery.
infographic.watch_item: Practical use depends on mature fault-tolerant quantum hardware, and meeting selected property targets does not automatically establish overall material stability.
infographic.paper_title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search

title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
authors: Apinya Ngoipala, Erik Fransson, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor
abstract: Lead-free halide perovskites based on Ge and Sn avoid the toxicity of Pb, but the two cations favor different structural distortions. The stereochemically active Ge $4s^2$ lone pair drives polar $B$-site off-centering, whereas the larger Sn$^{2+}$ cation favors octahedral tilting. Here, we map how these two instabilities compete across the full composition range of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential trained on hybrid-functional data. At low temperature the alloy exhibits a morphotropic phase boundary between $x=0.60$ and $0.65$ that separates a ferroelectric monoclinic $Cc$ phase from a monoclinic $P2_1$ phase with mixed antipolar and polar off-centering, with both the tilt pattern and the off-centering order changing discontinuously. The composition-temperature phase diagram reproduces the known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and reveals an intermediate tetragonal $I4/mcm$ phase near the boundary that has no counterpart in either parent compound. Above the transition temperatures the $B$ cations remain locally off-centered but orientationally disordered. The structural transition at the boundary causes a jump in the band gap at low temperature, whereas at $350$ K the gap decreases smoothly with Sn content. These results establish $B$-site mixing as a means to tune polar and rotational order in lead-free halide perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: Competing Ge-driven polar off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature phase boundary at x = 0.60–0.65 in lead-free CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃ alloys.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn composition offers a route to tune polar order, crystal structure, and band gap in lead-free halide perovskites.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across the full Ge/Sn composition range.
Map temperature-dependent tilting, off-centering, and structural phases.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and predict an intermediate tetragonal I4/mcm phase absent from either parent compound.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based alloy predictions; experimental validation of the phase boundary and intermediate phase remains necessary.
infographic.paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys

title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
authors: Feiyu Zhou, Wei Qiu, Fei Shuang, Yilun Liu, Shengying Yue, Penghua Ying
abstract: State-of-the-art atomistic foundation models provide broadly transferable energy and force predictions, but their direct deployment in large-scale molecular dynamics remains computationally costly. Here we examine whether their knowledge can be distilled into compact potentials while retaining the physical responses of heterogeneous semiconductor interfaces. From 128 pretrained models spanning 22 model families, we select a fixed EquiformerV3 teacher and train atomic cluster expansion (ACE) and neuroevolution potential (NEP) students without target-specific teacher fine-tuning, with both simulation speed and accessible system size improved by several orders of magnitude relative to the teacher model. Matched training configurations and architectures enable direct comparisons with students trained on density-functional-theory (DFT) reference labels. For 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces, direct distillation preserves termination-dependent thermal conductance and dominant spectral features, with conductance differing by at most 6.6% from DFT-trained counterparts. In 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens loaded at 500 K, tensile strength and loading work differ by 2.8% and 1.5%, respectively. Exploratory SiC/a-C/SiC simulations retain the principal thermal bottleneck and the direction of the annealing response. Furthermore, a four-model committee retrieves 42-56% of the highest-error teacher configurations with a 10% selection budget and improves high-error force fitting, but does not consistently improve downstream properties. These findings demonstrate that direct distillation can preserve key interfacial thermal and mechanical responses in compact interatomic potentials, opening a path towards large-scale, high-throughput simulations of heterogeneous interfaces.

infographic.key_insight: Compact ACE and NEP potentials distilled from a fixed atomistic foundation model preserve key semiconductor-interface responses while enabling simulations several orders of magnitude faster and larger than the teacher.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Direct distillation offers a practical route to large-scale thermal and mechanical simulations of heterogeneous interfaces without target-specific teacher fine-tuning.
method: Select an EquiformerV3 teacher from 128 pretrained models across 22 families.
Distill teacher predictions into compact ACE and NEP potentials.
Compare with DFT-trained students using matched training configurations and architectures.
infographic.evidence_signal: Against DFT-trained counterparts, distilled models differ by at most 6.6% in thermal conductance for 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces and by 2.8% in tensile strength and 1.5% in loading work for 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens at 500 K.
infographic.watch_item: Committee-based selection improves high-error force fitting but does not consistently improve downstream properties, so interface-level validation remains essential.
infographic.paper_title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces

title: Edge-scaling softening of a universal machine-learned potential: point-defect formation energies in a coronene graphene quantum dot
authors: Andrii Tuzhykov, Vladimir Soloviev, Arnold Kiv, Andrii Bielinskyi
abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are increasingly used as computationally efficient surrogates for density functional theory (DFT) in high-throughput nanomaterials screening. Systematic softening has been reported for several universal MLIPs when high-energy and far-from-equilibrium configurations are underrepresented in training data. We examine how this behavior appears at under-coordinated edge sites in graphene quantum dots (GQDs), where a vacancy can have pronounced molecular-radical character. Using coronene (C$_{24}$H$_{12}$), a hexagonal GQD with $D_{6h}$ symmetry and three carbon classes, we benchmark SevenNet (7net-omni-i12) against spin-polarized PBE DFT (GPAW) for monovacancy, divacancy, and Stone-Wales defects. Beyond the full site- and bond-resolved landscapes, we perform a controlled matched-reconstruction comparison in which 28 vacancy and divacancy configurations are scored by both engines using self-consistent chemical-potential reservoirs. In this dataset, SevenNet underestimates all 28 vacancy and divacancy formation energies, and the mean deficit increases with under-coordination within each defect family: 0.30-0.74 eV for monovacancies and 0.65-1.11 eV for divacancies as the number of broken edge C-H bonds increases. By contrast, the mean Stone-Wales energies differ by only 0.013 eV. SevenNet also preserves the ordering of three hydrogen-dependent reconstruction basins and reproduces $D_{6h}$-equivalent sites to within a few meV. The within-class symmetry spread therefore provides a practical diagnostic of basin-sensitive relaxations. Within the present coronene benchmark, these results support MLIP-based structure screening and preliminary ranking, while absolute vacancy energies and multi-basin edge configurations still require DFT validation.

infographic.key_insight: SevenNet systematically underestimates vacancy formation energies in coronene, with larger deficits at increasingly under-coordinated edges, while closely matching mean Stone–Wales energies.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Universal MLIPs can accelerate graphene quantum-dot structure screening, but absolute vacancy energies and complex edge reconstructions still need DFT validation.
method: Benchmark SevenNet against spin-polarized PBE DFT for defects in coronene (C24H12).
Map site- and bond-resolved monovacancy, divacancy, and Stone–Wales energetics.
Compare 28 matched vacancy reconstructions using self-consistent chemical-potential reservoirs.
infographic.evidence_signal: SevenNet underestimates all 28 matched vacancy energies; mean deficits increase with broken edge C–H bonds from 0.30 to 0.74 eV for monovacancies and 0.65 to 1.11 eV for divacancies, versus a 0.013 eV difference in mean Stone–Wales energy.
infographic.watch_item: Evidence is limited to coronene; monitor symmetry-equivalent energy spreads for basin-sensitive relaxations and validate multi-basin edge configurations with DFT.
infographic.paper_title: Edge-scaling softening of a universal machine-learned potential: point-defect formation energies in a coronene graphene quantum dot

title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study
authors: Paawan Chandrakanth, Nikos Ch. Karayiannis, Subhalaxmi Das, Supriya Roy
abstract: Demixing through liquid-liquid phase separation is relevant to nanoparticle (NP) aggregation in polymer nanocomposites (PNCs), biomolecular compartmentalization, and liquids embedded in elastic networks. Mixing-demixing phase behavior depends on factors, such as particle size distribution, system dimen-sionality, intermolecular interactions, and relative concentrations. Here, using Langevin Dynamics simu-lations, we systematically investigate the effect of inter-nanoparticle repulsion on the self-assembly of PNCs under extreme confinement. A nanoparticle assembly, in the form of a compact droplet, is immersed in a polymer matrix of semiflexible, rod-like chains. By varying the nanoparticle-nanoparticle repulsion strength, while fixing all other interactions, we identify four distinct regimes with respect to the self-assembled NP morphologies: droplet, slab, crystalline droplet, and dispersed. Cluster-based analysis reveals a progressive loss of nanoparticle droplet integrity, leading to fragmentation within the dispersed regime. Local order of the nanoparticle assembly and global order of polymer chains are gauged through refined descriptors, quantifying the degrees of crystallinity and of nematic order, respectively. Interest-ingly, the slab regime exhibits negligible nanoparticle crystallization yet demonstrates the strongest polymer nematic ordering. In contrast, the crystalline droplet displays extensive triangular close-packed crystallites accompanied by a significant reduction in polymer nematic order, owing to its rhomboid shape. In the dispersed regime, nanoparticle fragmentation facilitates efficient mixing and local smectic-like ordering of the polymer chains. These findings demonstrate that fine-tuning inter-NP repulsions can control self-organization and the resulting morphologies, providing insights into PNCs with tailored functionality.

infographic.key_insight: Tuning inter-nanoparticle repulsion produces four morphologies—droplet, slab, crystalline droplet, and dispersed—with distinct effects on polymer ordering.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Interparticle repulsion offers a potential design lever for controlling nanoparticle dispersion and polymer organization in confined polymer nanocomposites.
method: Langevin dynamics simulations of nanoparticles in a semiflexible, rod-like polymer matrix under extreme confinement.
Varied nanoparticle–nanoparticle repulsion while holding other interactions fixed.
Analyzed nanoparticle clustering, local crystallinity, and polymer nematic order.
infographic.evidence_signal: The slab regime showed the strongest polymer nematic order despite negligible nanoparticle crystallization, while crystalline droplets reduced nematic order and dispersed nanoparticles enabled local smectic-like ordering.
infographic.watch_item: Results concern an extremely confined simulation model; transferability to bulk materials or experimental systems remains to be established.
infographic.paper_title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study

title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials
authors: Yuewen Huang, Pin Chen, Yutong Lu
abstract: Accurate prediction of electronic Hamiltonians would enable broad property inference while avoiding the high computational cost of Density Functional Theory (DFT). However, progress toward general-purpose materials foundation models is limited by a data bottleneck: existing Hamiltonian datasets are typically small, lack structural diversity, and often omit essential relativistic physics such as spin--orbit coupling (SOC). We therefore construct UniHam, a large-scale Hamiltonian dataset and benchmark suite comprising 100,000+ DFT-computed complex-valued Hermitian Hamiltonians with full SOC, covering 72 elements and a wide range of crystal geometries and symmetries (spanning diverse lattice types and space-group families). Building on UniHam, we benchmark two representative state-of-the-art models under a standardized protocol and introduce complementary evaluation metrics that jointly assess three dimensions: (i) Hamiltonian reconstruction accuracy, (ii) out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization across composition/symmetry shifts, and (iii) the ability to support downstream property prediction from the predicted Hamiltonians. Experiments on UniHam demonstrate that the proposed benchmark and metrics effectively differentiate model capabilities, revealing intrinsic SOC- and element-dependent failure modes, large variations in compositional OOD robustness, and the necessity of spectral-level evaluation to assess whether Hamiltonian predictions reliably support downstream electronic-structure properties. Overall, UniHam provides a reproducible, SOC-complete benchmark that can sharpen model comparisons and accelerate the development of next-generation foundation models for quantum materials.

infographic.key_insight: UniHam provides 100,000+ DFT-computed Hamiltonians with full spin–orbit coupling (SOC) to benchmark AI models for electronic-structure prediction.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Learning Hamiltonians could reduce reliance on costly DFT calculations while supporting downstream electronic-property prediction for materials design.
method: Assemble complex-valued Hermitian Hamiltonians covering 72 elements and diverse crystal geometries and symmetries.
Benchmark two representative state-of-the-art models under a standardized protocol.
Evaluate reconstruction accuracy, composition/symmetry OOD generalization, and downstream property prediction.
infographic.evidence_signal: The benchmark reveals SOC- and element-dependent failure modes, substantial variation in compositional OOD robustness, and the need for spectral-level evaluation.
infographic.watch_item: Low Hamiltonian reconstruction error alone does not establish reliable downstream electronic-property predictions.
infographic.paper_title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials

title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
authors: Donggeun Kang, Seongju Lee, Yonggoon Jeon
abstract: Iodine-vacancy migration and association are important factors in the structural stability of halide perovskites. Although neighboring vacancies have been suggested to form energetically favorable pairs, their stability and reconfiguration under finite-temperature lattice deformation remain unclear. Here, we combine machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) and density functional theory (DFT) to investigate neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3 under isotropic and biaxial strain. The MLMD trajectories reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of short-time hopping fractions on strain, with strong isotropic compression favoring point-like separation and tension promoting pair-preserving relay hopping. Notably, biaxial compression produces distinct orientation-dependent responses: vacancy pairs initially aligned with the compressed plane preferentially undergo separation, whereas those perpendicular to the plane predominantly exhibit relay hopping. Complementary static calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential yield repulsive interactions for all configurations examined. These findings highlight the importance of finite-temperature dynamics and strain-dependent local geometry in understanding vacancy-pair stability and reconfiguration in halide perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: Strain controls iodine-vacancy pair dynamics in CsPbI3: strong isotropic compression favors separation, tension promotes pair-preserving relay hopping, and biaxial compression produces orientation-dependent behavior.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Strain and vacancy-pair orientation may offer design variables for managing defect migration and structural stability in halide perovskites.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies under isotropic and biaxial strain.
Analysis of short-time hopping, pair separation, and relay motion.
Static vacancy-interaction calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential.
infographic.evidence_signal: MLMD shows nonmonotonic strain-dependent hopping fractions, while DFT and SevenNet-0 yield repulsive vacancy interactions for every configuration examined.
infographic.watch_item: Short-time hopping behavior does not establish long-term vacancy-pair stability or device-scale reliability.
infographic.paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study

title: Bulk CMSX-4 Single-Crystal Builds via Laser-Directed Energy Deposition: Epitaxial Stability and Microstructure Evolution
authors: Divya Nalajala, Swapnil Bhure, R. Ajithkannan, Shubhang Galagali, Abhik Choudhury
abstract: Single-crystal processing of Ni-based superalloys using laser-directed energy deposition (L-DED) is extremely challenging, given the interplay of a number of processing parameters. In this work, we develop strategies to maintain single-crystal growth in long cylindrical rod geometries by combining dynamic adjustment of laser power, informed by in-situ infrared thermal feedback, with a simulation-guided external cooling system. This combined approach ensures optimal heat extraction during additive manufacturing, maintaining near-steady-state conditions at the solidification interface and extending continuous epitaxial growth to nearly twice the build height achievable through process control alone. The developed strategy results in continuous single-crystal growth, as validated by electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). The steady-state nature of solidification is revealed through the near-constant primary dendritic arm spacing. Further, the heat-treatment is optimized by reducing the solutionizing time (by 47\%), resulting in faster eutectic dissolution. Comparison of the aged microstructures reveals a similar distribution of precipitates between the classical Bridgman- and L-DED-processed samples.

infographic.key_insight: Combining infrared-feedback laser power control with simulation-guided external cooling sustained epitaxial CMSX-4 growth to nearly twice the build height achieved with process control alone.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Improved heat extraction enables taller single-crystal superalloy builds by L-DED, while optimized heat treatment reduces solutionizing time by 47%.
method: Dynamically adjust laser power using in-situ infrared thermal feedback.
Apply simulation-guided external cooling to stabilize solidification in cylindrical rods.
Optimize heat treatment and compare aged L-DED microstructures with Bridgman-processed samples.
infographic.evidence_signal: EBSD validated continuous single-crystal growth, near-constant primary dendrite arm spacing indicated steady solidification, and aged samples showed similar precipitate distributions across processing routes.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract demonstrates long cylindrical rods; scalability to complex geometries and resulting mechanical performance remain unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: Bulk CMSX-4 Single-Crystal Builds via Laser-Directed Energy Deposition: Epitaxial Stability and Microstructure Evolution

title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram
authors: Raymundo Arróyave
abstract: Knowledge of phase stability is the first requirement for materials design, and predicting the conditions under which new materials can be synthesized has become a key capability of self-driving laboratories (SDLs). For inorganic materials, notably alloys, these predictions come from thermodynamic databases built with the CALPHAD method. Building a database, however, requires expert judgment at many steps, and because these decisions are rarely recorded, others can use a database but cannot regenerate or update it. Machines can already collect the data, build a first model with machine-learned interatomic potentials and refine it against experiments. The assessment itself, the sequence of judgments that turns these parts into a reliable database, is still carried out by human experts. We argue that it can be automated reproducibly only if the expert knowledge behind an assessment is encoded in formal protocols, so that an assessment delivers a record of its construction and not only its parameters. We introduce ORCHID-SAGE, a standard that organizes this record into reproducible and automatable protocols. In this first attempt, applied to Cr-Ni, the database was regenerated from its record by a script on a second machine, by an AI agent working only through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and by a refit from public sources only, with the same predictions. Recorded in this way, a database need no longer be fixed at publication but can be updated by AI agents as SDLs and other sources provide new evidence, while the judgment remains with people and on the record.

infographic.key_insight: ORCHID-SAGE formalizes expert CALPHAD assessment decisions into protocols so thermodynamic databases can be regenerated from their construction records, not just reused.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Reproducible, updateable phase-stability databases could support alloy design and synthesis planning in self-driving laboratories.
method: Encode expert assessment judgments in formal, reproducible protocols.
Record the evidence and decisions used to construct a CALPHAD database.
Test regeneration through scripting, an MCP-only AI agent, and refitting from public sources.
infographic.evidence_signal: In the initial Cr–Ni application, regeneration on a second machine, an MCP-only AI agent, and a public-source refit produced the same predictions.
infographic.watch_item: Validation is limited to the initial Cr–Ni case; broader applicability and reliable updates with new evidence remain to be demonstrated.
infographic.paper_title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram

title: Evidential Deep Regression for Universal Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian Models
authors: Jiaxuan Liu, Yan Zhang, Caiyuan Ye, Tiannian Zhu, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng
abstract: Universal density functional theory (DFT) Hamiltonian models trained across broad chemical and structural spaces offer an efficient route from atomic structure to electronic properties. However, estimating prediction uncertainty alongside fast Hamiltonian predictions remains a challenge. In this work, we present EviDTB, an evidential deep regression approach for tight-binding DFT Hamiltonians that effectively estimates prediction uncertainty in a single forward pass. Compared with deep ensembles, Monte Carlo dropout, and mean-variance estimation (MVE), EviDTB achieves a better balance between computational cost and uncertainty-quantification performance. On 5,478 held-out test structures, EviDTB achieves a full spin--orbit-coupled (SOC) Hamiltonian matrix-element mean absolute error of 0.622meV. Its mean uncertainty per atom correlates with the mean local squared prediction error (Spearman $ρ=0.812$); removing the 15% most uncertain structures reduces the 99th percentile of this error by 78%, from 16.63 to 3.72eV$^2$. This score offers a practical way to prioritize candidates for first-principles verification. We hope that combining fast Hamiltonian prediction with uncertainty-guided screening will accelerate the search for materials with desirable electronic properties.

infographic.key_insight: EviDTB predicts DFT Hamiltonians and estimates their uncertainty in a single forward pass, enabling uncertainty-guided materials screening.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Uncertainty scores can help prioritize materials for first-principles verification while reducing reliance on potentially unreliable predictions.
method: Applies evidential deep regression to tight-binding DFT Hamiltonian prediction.
Estimates prediction uncertainty without repeated inference passes.
Reports a better cost–uncertainty-performance balance than deep ensembles, Monte Carlo dropout, and mean-variance estimation.
infographic.evidence_signal: On 5,478 held-out structures, EviDTB achieved 0.622 meV full-SOC Hamiltonian matrix-element MAE and uncertainty–error Spearman ρ = 0.812; excluding the 15% most uncertain structures reduced the 99th-percentile mean local squared error by 78%.
infographic.watch_item: Reliability on chemical and structural spaces beyond the reported held-out evaluation requires further validation.
infographic.paper_title: Evidential Deep Regression for Universal Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian Models

title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
authors: Xuyu Dong, Yixuan Li, Jianguo Huang, Feng Chen, Yiyun Zhou, Bo An
abstract: Large language models and the multi-agent systems built around them could accelerate materials discovery by connecting scientific knowledge with experimental decisions. Existing benchmarks establish capabilities in domain knowledge, multimodal interpretation and scientific tool use. As language models increasingly support materials research workflows, their ability to distinguish closely related material states and reason accurately with quantitative evidence remains insufficiently evaluated. These abilities are essential for comparing material responses, assessing mechanisms and maintaining reliable judgements as experimental evidence accumulates. We introduce MatScope to evaluate three connected capabilities. M1 tests unaided, condition-specific reasoning through 200 tasks spanning ten research functions, using aluminium and high-entropy alloys as representative material systems. M2 tests agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions. MatEvoBench-20 tests initial forecasts across scientific dependency chains and revisions of still-hidden responses as observations accumulate. Across eleven model deployments, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, given-input calculations and many physical explanations are handled well. Fine-grained response estimates, comparisons between similar states and quantitatively supported choices remain substantially weaker. Related literature improves selected estimates, while condition and baseline mismatches limit transfer. Progressive observations calibrate some downstream responses and destabilize earlier accurate predictions. MatScope establishes measurable targets for developing reliable scientific reasoning in future self-evolving materials laboratories and materials-aware world models.

infographic.key_insight: MatScope finds that strong calculations and physical explanations do not guarantee reliable predictions or comparisons between closely related material states.
infographic.engineering_relevance: AI-assisted materials workflows need condition-matched evidence and quantitative checks before model predictions guide experimental decisions.
method: M1 tests unaided, condition-specific reasoning on 200 tasks across ten research functions using aluminium and high-entropy alloys.
M2 tests agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions.
MatEvoBench-20 tests forecasts across scientific dependency chains and revisions as observations accumulate.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across eleven model deployments, calculations from supplied inputs and many physical explanations performed well, while fine-grained estimates, similar-state comparisons and quantitatively supported choices remained weaker.
infographic.watch_item: Related literature can mismatch experimental conditions or baselines, and new observations can destabilize previously accurate predictions.
infographic.paper_title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories

title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection
authors: Gwangseon Jang, Sieun Yun, Dong Ho Lee, Kyong-Ha Lee, Chanuk Lim, Jin Woo Choi
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization remains a central challenge in materials property prediction, where models must extrapolate to novel chemistries beyond the training distribution. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong scientific reasoning, their direct use for quantitative prediction remains limited. To address this, we systematically evaluate multiple roles for LLM assistance, finding that only taxonomy-based grouping consistently improves OOD generalization over a strong kNN+GBT baseline. Building on this, we here propose MOTIF, a framework that leverages LLMs not as predictors, but as generators of candidate taxonomies that partition materials into chemically meaningful environments. These taxonomies are evaluated via training-only pseudo-OOD validation, and only those that improve generalization are retained. Invariant feature selection is then applied within each accepted taxonomy, followed by gated aggregation across taxonomies. We evaluate on 2D halide perovskites, where bandgap prediction must generalize across distinct organic spacer families. On this benchmark, MOTIF reduces mean OOD MAE from 0.122 to 0.111 eV. Under a frozen dev/test protocol, the deployable configuration further improves errors from 0.123 to 0.117 eV (electronic bandgap) and from 0.181 to 0.173 eV (optical bandgap). Beyond this primary task, we validate transferability across additional materials datasets, including 3D perovskite solar cell efficiencies and Matbench benchmarks with structure-based splits. Across domains, MOTIF consistently improves robustness under distribution shift, outperforming expert-defined groupings, rule-based heuristics, and clustering baselines, while remaining competitive with strong classical selection methods. These results demonstrate that LLMs are most effective not as predictors, but as tools for discovering structure in data.

infographic.key_insight: MOTIF improves out-of-distribution materials property prediction by using LLMs to propose chemical taxonomies rather than predict numerical properties directly.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Taxonomy-guided feature selection can make property models more robust when screening materials with chemistries beyond the training distribution.
method: Generate candidate material taxonomies with LLMs.
Retain taxonomies that improve training-only pseudo-OOD validation.
Apply invariant feature selection within each taxonomy and gated aggregation across taxonomies.
infographic.evidence_signal: On 2D halide perovskites, mean OOD bandgap MAE fell from 0.122 to 0.111 eV; frozen dev/test evaluation also showed smaller gains for electronic and optical bandgaps, with transfer evaluated on additional materials datasets.
infographic.watch_item: Taxonomy selection depends on pseudo-OOD validation, whose shifts may not represent genuinely novel deployment chemistries.
infographic.paper_title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection

title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
authors: Lucy Liu, Leon M. Kamp, Katia Bertoldi, L. Mahadevan
abstract: Automatic differentiation has enabled rapid progress on continuous-variable mechanical design problems, but gradient-based optimization still struggles with discrete variables. The standard approach is to optimize using a continuous relaxation of the choices, then commit to the nearest discrete design at the end. Why this procedure selects unfavorable basins is poorly understood. Here, we introduce a practical, interpretable design problem inspired by origami, in which automatic differentiation is used to design shapes with a target functional behavior. Each origami sheet has a fixed geometry, and a bilevel optimization framework tunes which one of four discrete hinge types to place at each fold. Baseline gradient-based design settles into basins with a large discretization gap: relaxed optimization solves 97% of runs, but the final, discrete solutions succeed only half the time. We find that the gap can be relieved with a surprisingly simple modification. An initialization prior uniformly biased toward the stiff, flat hinge option boosts the final solve fraction from 49% to 69%. Applying the prior adds no additional compute and leaves the optimization process unchanged. Compared to the baseline, sheets produced with the prior have greater geometric compatibility and mechanical stiffness. Directly penalizing frustration and floppiness in the outer loss function produces an even greater improvement than the prior does, raising the solve fraction to 78% and indicating that these properties help distinguish the unfavorable basins. Our results demonstrate that loss landscapes for mechanical design can have physically meaningful basins that are not robust to discretization and cause solves to fail. Targeting these basins' physical signatures, even with just an initialization bias, helps avoid them.

infographic.key_insight: Biasing initialization toward stiff, flat hinges helps gradient-based origami design avoid physically unfavorable basins and improves success after discretization.
infographic.engineering_relevance: A no-extra-compute initialization change can improve discrete mechanical designs, while penalties targeting geometric incompatibility and floppiness offer further gains.
method: Use automatic differentiation in bilevel optimization to assign four discrete hinge types on fixed origami geometries.
Bias the continuous relaxation’s initialization toward the stiff, flat hinge option.
Alternatively, penalize frustration and floppiness in the outer design loss.
infographic.evidence_signal: Relaxed optimization solved 97% of baseline runs, but discrete success was 49%; the initialization prior raised discrete success to 69%, and physical penalties raised it to 78%.
infographic.watch_item: The reported gains concern fixed-geometry origami design; transfer to other discrete mechanical systems remains to be established.
infographic.paper_title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design

title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
authors: Minh Nghia Nguyen, Beate Paulus, Akhil S. Nair
abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties. Our results show that the effectiveness of data acquisition strategies depend strongly on the interplay between the model, dataset, and prediction task, although uncertainty-based sampling generally outperforms alternative strategies. Based on these findings, we derive guidelines for selecting data acquisition strategies under a given labelling budget.

infographic.key_insight: Uncertainty-based sampling generally improves training-data acquisition, but the best strategy depends on the model, dataset, and prediction task.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Task-specific data acquisition can help allocate limited labelling budgets more efficiently for molecular and materials property prediction.
method: Compare random sampling with multiple active learning strategies.
Evaluate across model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties.
Derive strategy-selection guidelines for a given labelling budget.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across diverse modelling settings, with uncertainty-based sampling generally outperforming alternatives, but provides no quantitative gains.
infographic.watch_item: Validate acquisition strategies in the intended prediction setting rather than assuming one approach will perform best universally.
infographic.paper_title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction

title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
authors: Manish Kumar, Bridget S. Ferris, Avital Isakov, Robert B. Wexler
abstract: The function of oxide materials, from solid-oxide fuel cells to solar thermochemical fuel production, depends on their oxygen vacancies. Their formation energetics have been mapped systematically for ternary perovskites, but reported values for the binary oxides, their conceptual and thermochemical building blocks, remain scattered across studies with differing computational methods. Here we report a systematic r$^2$SCAN density functional theory survey of neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies across 39 binary main-group metal oxide polymorphs spanning groups 1, 2, 13, 14, and 15, using the ShakeNBreak method to locate reconstructed defect ground states. The formation energies span 8 eV and decrease down each group and, for most multivalent cations, with increasing oxidation state. Both trends follow the reducibility of the cation. An interpretable crystal feature model is fit to these energies; its inputs are properties of the pristine bulk, with the reduction potential alternatively taken from tabulated thermochemistry. Retaining only its two dominant descriptors, the crystal reduction potential and the band gap, the model reproduces the formation energies with a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV, lower than that of its four-descriptor parent model for transition-metal perovskites. The bond-breaking and stability terms of the full Born-Haber fit prove statistically null for the binary oxides, and the largest residuals identify the hosts where electron accommodation departs from the cation-reduction picture that the descriptors encode. The dataset provides a benchmark for machine-learning interatomic potentials, and the model estimates vacancy formation energies of main-group oxides from bulk properties alone.

infographic.key_insight: Oxygen vacancy formation energies across binary main-group metal oxides largely track cation reducibility and can be predicted using crystal reduction potential and band gap.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Bulk-property predictions could accelerate oxide screening for solid-oxide fuel cells and solar thermochemical fuel production.
method: Survey 39 oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Use ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed neutral-vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model and retain its two dominant descriptors.
infographic.evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
infographic.watch_item: The model is evaluated on neutral vacancies in main-group oxides; its largest residuals flag cases where electron accommodation departs from cation reduction.
infographic.paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides

title: High-Fidelity In Silico Dataset of Ordered Binary and Ternary MXenes with Predictive Synthesis Guidance
authors: Ahmed H. Biby, Charles B. Musgrave
abstract: Despite their promise, the targeted synthesis of novel MXenes remains challenging due to their vast structural and compositional space and the lack of reliable stability descriptors that account for synthesis conditions. To address this gap, we utilized density functional theory (DFT) with the r$^2$SCAN functional to develop a high-fidelity dataset of 1,040 ordered binary and ternary bare delaminated MXenes, including mono-transition metal MXenes, in-plane ordered double-transition metal MXenes, in-plane ordered metal-divacancy MXenes, and out-of-plane ordered double-transition-metal MXenes. For each structure, we calculated formation and decomposition Gibbs energies, decomposition products, layer symmetry groups, and energies above the hull. We find that all MXenes are thermodynamically inaccessible under equilibrium conditions. However, 115 predominantly carbide MXenes become thermodynamically stabilized at elevated temperatures (500--2000 K), and 23 are stabilized under high pressure (10 GPa). Additionally, three MXenes in the Mn--Fe--C chemical space are stabilized within an experimentally feasible range of carbon chemical potentials. These findings reveal stability trends across the MXene space and identify synthesis strategies that can guide experimental efforts. Our dataset provides a robust foundation for developing machine-learned stability descriptors and for guiding experimental efforts toward novel MXene discovery. By identifying synthesizable candidates along with their synthesis conditions, this work bridges a critical gap in data-driven approaches to MXene discovery and lays the foundation for future autonomous experimental workflows.

infographic.key_insight: DFT screening identifies condition-dependent routes to stabilize otherwise equilibrium-inaccessible MXenes, offering targeted synthesis guidance.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The dataset helps prioritize MXene candidates and synthesis conditions while providing a foundation for machine-learned stability descriptors.
method: Calculated 1,040 ordered binary and ternary bare delaminated MXenes using r²SCAN DFT.
Computed formation and decomposition Gibbs energies, decomposition products, layer symmetries, and energies above the hull.
Evaluated stability under elevated temperature, high pressure, and varying carbon chemical potential.
infographic.evidence_signal: The calculations predict stabilization of 115 predominantly carbide MXenes at 500–2000 K, 23 at 10 GPa, and three Mn–Fe–C MXenes within experimentally feasible carbon chemical potentials.
infographic.watch_item: Predicted thermodynamic stabilization does not establish experimental synthesizability; kinetics and surface terminations absent from the bare-MXene models may affect outcomes.
infographic.paper_title: High-Fidelity In Silico Dataset of Ordered Binary and Ternary MXenes with Predictive Synthesis Guidance

title: Stable ring-polymer molecular dynamics without Fourier transforms: a linear-scaling bead-space Cayley propagator
authors: Yuhao Chen, Yongle Li, Xiao He
abstract: Ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) builds zero-point energy and tunnelling into classical trajectories and is widely used for bimolecular rate coefficients. At low temperature it requires many beads, and the stiff ring-polymer springs then limit the integrator. The Cayley modification of the free ring-polymer step removes this limit, but it has so far been formulated mode by mode, which requires Fourier transforms of every degree of freedom at every step. Here we show that, in bead coordinates, the Cayley step reduces to one cyclic tridiagonal solve for the midpoint of the step, with a matrix that depends only on the number of beads $P$, the temperature and the time step, and not on the atomic masses. The bead-space step is exactly the normal-mode Cayley map: it conserves the free ring-polymer energy, preserves the free ring-polymer Boltzmann distribution, and is stable for any $P$ whenever $ΩΔt<2$ for the highest physical frequency $Ω$. A Thomas recursion with a rank-two Woodbury correction solves it in about $18P$ operations per degree of freedom without pivoting, with a condition number bounded by $1+(ω_PΔt)^2$, and the inverse matrix decays geometrically with bead separation, so the step is local in bead index. Implemented in the open-source PyRPMD package, the propagator reproduces normal-mode Cayley to $1.5\times10^{-15}$ for up to 2048 beads and its cost grows linearly with $P$. For direct RPMD (dRPMD), which has so far integrated the springs explicitly, these properties raise the stability limit on the time step 23--29-fold in published low-temperature settings; at \SI{20}{K} with 3072 beads, the Cayley step conserves the ring-polymer energy as well as velocity Verlet does with a time step about ten times larger, while leaving the low-lying internal modes that govern spurious resonances essentially unchanged.

infographic.key_insight: A bead-space Cayley propagator removes Fourier transforms from RPMD spring integration while exactly reproducing the normal-mode Cayley map at linear cost.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The method can accelerate low-temperature molecular reaction simulations that require many ring-polymer beads without sacrificing free ring-polymer energy conservation.
method: Replace mode-by-mode propagation with one cyclic tridiagonal midpoint solve using a mass-independent matrix.
Apply Thomas recursion with a rank-two Woodbury correction in about 18P operations per degree of freedom.
Implement the propagator in the open-source PyRPMD package.
infographic.evidence_signal: Tests reproduce normal-mode Cayley to 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ for up to 2048 beads, show linear cost scaling, and indicate 23–29-fold higher timestep stability limits in published low-temperature dRPMD settings.
infographic.watch_item: Stability still requires ΩΔt < 2 for the highest physical frequency, and low-lying internal modes associated with spurious resonances remain essentially unchanged.
infographic.paper_title: Stable ring-polymer molecular dynamics without Fourier transforms: a linear-scaling bead-space Cayley propagator
